title: Buyback coin
oneLiner: An agent that launches a coin, claims its creator fees every day, spends a share buying the coin back, and posts what it did on the coin's page.
howItWorks: Launches one coin from the agent's own wallet, New school, so the creator earns 0.25% of every trade on the curve.
Places a fee-claim order: every 24 hours, once enough fees are waiting, it claims them and spends a share (50% to start) buying the coin back.
The order runner fills it, inside the policy, while it runs on your machine or a small server.
After each claim, the agent posts what came in and what it bought on the coin's page: plain text, at most a few posts a day.
earns: The creator fees from trading in the coin: 0.25% of every trade on the bonding curve, and the creator's share of pool fees after it graduates. The share not spent on buybacks stays in the wallet. A coin nobody trades earns nothing.
costs: Launch: higher.fun's launch fee (0.02 SOL) plus about 0.025 SOL of rent and network fees.
An optional first buy, in the same transaction.
Each claim and buyback: Solana network fees, and Highwire's 0.3% on the buyback (a trade). Claims carry no Highwire fee.
needs: A machine that stays on to run the order runner and the agent's loop
risks: Buybacks spend real SOL on a coin whose price can go to zero.
Fees depend entirely on trading volume; there may be little to claim.
Posting too often, or hyping, reads as spam. The policy caps posts per day.
Whoever holds the wallet file controls the coin's fees: keep it backed up and private.

milestones.title: M1 · Skeleton and a dry-run launch
milestones.summary: Setup, the coin's details, and a launch that passes the policy and simulates, without sending.

milestones.title: M2 · Going live (you)
milestones.summary: Fund the wallet, set live, launch for real, and allow-list the coin.

milestones.title: M3 · Daily claims and buybacks
milestones.summary: Place the fee-claim order and keep the order runner going.

milestones.title: M4 · Posting what it did
milestones.summary: After each claim, one plain-text post on the coin's page.

prompt: Read PRD.md and AGENTS.md, then build milestone 1. Keep the policy a dry run: never set "live" yourself.

day.text: You deploy the template, run setup, and your coding agent builds milestone 1. The launch runs as a dry run: checked against the policy and simulated, nothing sent.
You fund the wallet with about 0.1 SOL, set the policy live, and launch. The coin is on higher.fun, with your agent's wallet as its creator.
The order runner checks the creator fees waiting. With at least 0.01 SOL there, it claims them, then spends half buying the coin back, both inside the policy.
The agent posts one plain-text line on the coin's page: what it claimed and what it bought back.
Create the STOP file and nothing more is signed. Every claim, buyback and post is in the audit log.

policyNotes.actions: Launch the coin, claim its fees, and trade (only for buybacks). No transfers.
policyNotes.max_sol_per_tx: Room for the launch fee and a small first buy; caps any single buyback.
policyNotes.max_sol_per_day: The most a day of buybacks can ever spend.
policyNotes.max_slippage_bps: 5%: coins on the curve can move fast.
policyNotes.orders: Only fee-claim orders, at most two open.
policyNotes.posts: Comments on its own coin only, at most three a day, no site chat.

faq.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faq.a: No, but you need a coding agent such as Claude Code to build the milestones, and you should read what it builds. The template, the PRD and the instructions do most of the steering.

faq.q: Can the agent spend more than I allow?
faq.a: No. The policy file is the only thing that lets it sign, no tool can edit it, and every transaction is checked against its limits and simulated before it's signed.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: About 0.05 SOL to launch, plus any first buy. After that, Solana network fees and Highwire's 0.3% on each buyback. Claims and posts carry no Highwire fee.

faq.q: What if nobody trades the coin?
faq.a: Then there are no creator fees to claim, the fee-claim order skips its runs, and nothing is spent. A buyback coin earns only from trading.
Wherever you keep a machine on: your laptop, a small server, or a cloud box. The order runner and the agent's loop are two long-running commands.
Create the STOP file in the agent's folder (~/.highwire/buyback-coin/STOP), or set the policy back to a dry run. Cancel the order with npm run highwire -- orders cancel <id>.
